papers.title: Reconfigurable generation of high-power structured light via nonlinear beam shaping
papers.abstract: High-power structured light has a wide range of applications, from material processing and high-capacity optical communications to programmable electron beams, plasmas, and nuclear states. On-demand generation of structured light and adaptive control of beam profiles are essential for many practical applications, but are difficult to achieve at high power. Here, we demonstrate reconfigurable generation of structured light from a high-power multimode-fiber laser amplifier through full-field control of a low-power seed. An efficient nonlinear beam shaping scheme based on a local linear approximation of the complex nonlinear input--output relation is developed and realized in situ. Diverse structured beams such as Gaussian, Bessel, vector and orbital angular momentum beams are directly generated from the fiber amplifier at powers exceeding 500 W. Our scheme enables real-time programmability of structured light and is readily scalable to even higher power levels. This work provides a general framework for controlling high-dimensional nonlinear systems without accurate knowledge or tractable model.

analysis.summary: 实现高功率光纤放大器中结构化光的可重构生成，通过非线性波束整形突破功率限制。
analysis.research思路: 解决高功率结构化光按需生成与自适应控制的难题，克服传统方法在高功率下的局限性。
analysis.experiment: 采用基于局部线性近似的高效非线性波束整形方案，通过低功率种子源全场控制实现。
analysis.innovation: 首次在高功率(>500W)光纤放大器中直接生成多种结构化光束，并实现实时可编程控制。
analysis.related_work: 包括空间光调制器波束整形、数字微镜器件控制、以及低功率结构化光生成技术。
analysis.impact: 为高功率结构化光应用开辟新途径，推动材料加工、光通信等领域的技术革新。

domain_trend.trend: 光通信与光纤传感正迈向高功率可重构、量子级集成与全功能感知网络新时代
domain_trend.development_direction: 光通信与光纤传感领域正从单一功能向多功能、高功率、量子级精度的智能集成系统发展，通过突破传统功率限制、实现量子级操作兼容性以及将普通光纤转变为多功能感知网络，为材料加工、量子通信、智能城市等领域提供革命性解决方案

papers.title: Release-free electro-optomechanical crystal modulator
papers.abstract: Electro-optic modulation is central to classical optical communications and emerging quantum technologies. High-confinement optomechanical crystal modulators enable microwave-optical transduction through strong optomechanical interactions and offer a promising interface between superconducting qubits and optical fibers. However, their performance is limited by thermal noise from optical absorption. Release-free optomechanical crystals provide improved thermal anchoring but have not yet been integrated into a microwave-optical transducer. Here, we demonstrate a release-free electro-optomechanical transducer combining strong optomechanical interactions in silicon with the efficient piezoelectricity of lithium niobate via micro-transfer printing. We observe electro- and optomechanical coupling rates compatible with quantum-level operation when co-integrated with a superconducting microwave circuit. This advance moves release-free electro-optomechanical devices toward practical microwave-optical interfaces.
